facts.statement: Katepensaurus lived during the Late Cretaceous in south-central Chubut Province, central Patagonia, Argentina.
facts.quote: known from the Late Cretaceous of south-central Chubut Province of central Patagonia, Argentina

facts.statement: The genus Katepensaurus contains only one known species, Katepensaurus goicoecheai.
facts.quote: It contains a single species, Katepensaurus goicoecheai

facts.statement: The only known specimen of Katepensaurus is the partial skeleton UNPSJB-PV 1007.
facts.quote: The holotype and only known specimen of Katepensaurus goicoecheai is UNPSJB-PV 1007, a partial skeleton

facts.statement: The individual represented by the holotype was at least seven years old and still growing when it died.
facts.quote: It represents an individual that was at least seven years old and had not finished growing when it died

facts.statement: The fossil-bearing Lower Member of the Bajo Barreal Formation dates to the Cenomanian or Turonian stages of the early Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: The Lower Member of the Bajo Barreal Formation is considered to date to the Cenomanian or Turonian age of the early Late Cretaceous

facts.statement: Katepensaurus was described as a new genus and species in 2013 by Lucio M. Ibiricu, Gabriel A. Casal, Rubén Dario Martínez, Matthew C. Lamanna, Marcelo Luna, and Leonardo Salgado.
facts.quote: In 2013, Lucio M. Ibiricu, Gabriel A. Casal, Rubén Dario Martínez, Matthew C. Lamanna, Marcelo Luna and Leonardo Salgado described this specimen as representing a new genus and species

facts.statement: The genus name Katepensaurus comes from the Tehuelche word for 'hole', referring to distinctive openings in the dorsal vertebrae.
facts.quote: The generic name is derived from Tehuelche katepenk, "hole", referring to a distinctive opening in the transverse processes of the dorsal vertebrae

facts.statement: The species name goicoecheai honors Alejandro Goicoechea, the owner of the ranch where the fossils were found.
facts.quote: The specific name honours Alejandro Goicoechea, the owner of the Estancia Laguna Palacios

facts.statement: Katepensaurus is unique among sauropods for having an additional set of pneumatic openings called laterodiapophyseal fenestrae.
facts.quote: Katepensaurus is unique among sauropods in exhibiting an additional set of pneumatic openings, termed laterodiapophyseal fenestrae

facts.statement: Katepensaurus possesses a unique pair of vertebral laminae not seen in any other rebbachisaurid.
facts.quote: Katepensaurus shows a unique pair of laminae, termed the dorsal parapophyseal centrodiapophyseal fossa lamina and the ventral parapophyseal centrodiapophyseal fossa lamina

facts.statement: Katepensaurus shows a mix of traits found in both nigersaurines/rebbachisaurines and limaysaurines.
facts.quote: Katepensaurus exhibits a combination of traits characteristic of nigersaurines/rebbachisaurines and traits characteristic of limaysaurines

facts.statement: It is debated whether Katepensaurus belongs to the limaysaurines or is a basal rebbachisaurid, as different studies have produced conflicting results.
facts.quote: Analyses by Mannion and colleagues in 2019 could not resolve the affinities of Katepensaurus precisely, and found differing results depending on their analysis protocol

facts.statement: Katepensaurus is classified within the family Rebbachisauridae.
Katepensaurus is placed in the subfamily Limaysaurinae.
Katepensaurus lived in the middle of the Cretaceous period, approximately 92 million years ago, between the Cenomanian and Turonian stages.
facts.quote: que vivió a mediados del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 92 millones de años entre el Cenomaniense y el Turoniense

facts.statement: Katepensaurus is assigned to Limaysaurinae, a family of diplodocoid rebbachisaurids.
facts.quote: Katepensaurus fue asignado a Limaysaurinae, una familia de diplodocoideos rebaquisáuridos

facts.statement: Katepensaurus lived during the Upper Cretaceous in the south-central part of Chubut Province, central Patagonia, Argentina.
facts.quote: Katepensaurus vivió durante el Cretácico Superior en la zona sur-central de la provincia de Chubut en el centro de la Patagonia, Argentina

facts.statement: The parent group of Katepensaurus is the family Rebbachisauridae.
Katepensaurus lived from 100.5 to 89.8 million years ago, spanning the Cenomanian to Turonian stages.
facts.quote: Time range: Cenomanian to Turonian (100.5 to 89.8 million years ago)
